skill.name: names-to-prospects
skill.description: Match names and companies to Leadsets records. Export current roles, companies, and work emails when available, with separate groups for verified addresses, catch-all addresses, and rows that need review.

security_audit.summary: The Leadsets endpoint supports external searches and enrichment, which disclose search filters and matched contact identifiers to the provider. The other static alerts are documentation, links, or workflow labels, with no evidence of shell execution, environment access, or host reconnaissance. The export can copy unnecessary personal data, and untrusted text may be interpreted as formulas by spreadsheet software.

remediation.suggestion: Before processing, disclose the Leadsets destination and fields sent. Confirm the user approves the transfer and send only the fields required for each lookup.

remediation.issue: Extra source columns are exported by default
remediation.suggestion: Export only required columns by default. Ask the user to approve any extra columns and confirm the destination and its sharing settings before writing.
Write untrusted text as literal values in Google Sheets. Sanitize formula-like values for CSV exports and test them in supported spreadsheet applications.

content.user_title: Enrich Contact Lists From Names and Companies
content.value_statement: Event lists often lack current job details and reliable work emails. This skill checks records in Leadsets and separates verified contacts from uncertain matches.
actual_capabilities: Read full names and companies from a CSV, Google Sheet, or pasted rows, and remove exact duplicates.
Use company domains and optional job titles or countries to narrow searches and flag ambiguous matches.
Estimate lookup usage and check Leadsets limits before processing the list.
Retrieve current roles, companies, and available work emails for matched people.
Flag people who changed companies and keep both the original and current company.
Export verified, catch-all, and review groups as CSV files or a Google Sheet.
limitations: Requires a Leadsets account and a connected Leadsets MCP server or REST API access.
Requires full names and companies. It does not guess email addresses or choose between ambiguous matches.
Search and enrichment quotas can limit how many rows are processed. Some contacts have no verified work email.
It does not send emails, add contacts to a sequence, or write to a CRM.

use_cases.title: Review webinar registrations
use_cases.description: Match an approved webinar list and separate verified contacts from registrations that need more research.

use_cases.title: Prepare a booth contact list
use_cases.description: Turn approved booth scans into a CSV with current roles and verified work emails where available.

use_cases.title: Check company changes
use_cases.description: Review an older list for job changes and route unresolved matches to a separate review group.

prompt_templates.title: Check a short contact list
prompt_templates.prompt: Match these approved name and company rows in Leadsets. List any names you cannot match confidently.

prompt_templates.title: Export an approved event list
prompt_templates.prompt: Enrich this approved event CSV. Export verified, catch-all, and review rows separately. Do not include extra source columns.

prompt_templates.title: Review company changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the supplied domains and titles to narrow matches. Flag people who moved and show both companies. Keep ambiguous matches in review.

prompt_templates.title: Process a list within quota
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate usage for this approved list before any lookup. Share the estimate and wait for approval. Process priority rows first and report any rows left.

output_examples.input: An approved webinar list with 12 rows, including two duplicates.
output: 10 unique rows: 6 verified, 1 catch-all, and 3 needing review.
The review group contains one ambiguous match, one missing match, and one person who changed companies.

output_examples.input: An older event list with a contact whose employer changed.
output: Needs review: Jordan Lee appears to have moved from Oakmere Systems to Elmbridge Labs.
Both companies are recorded. The row is excluded from the verified group.

best_practices: Confirm you may share contact details with Leadsets before running lookups.
Include reliable company domains or job titles when people or companies have similar names.
Remove unnecessary source columns first and confirm who can access the export.
anti_patterns: Treating a verified email address as consent to contact the person.
Selecting an ambiguous match or using a guessed email address.
Exporting sensitive attendee fields to a shared sheet without checking access.

faq.question: What input does the skill need?
faq.answer: Provide full names and companies in a CSV, Google Sheet, or pasted rows. Domains, titles, and countries are optional.

faq.question: Do I need a Leadsets account?
faq.answer: Yes. Connect the Leadsets MCP server to your agent or provide REST API access through your agent's credential settings.

faq.question: What counts as a verified work email?
faq.answer: Leadsets must report that address as verified. Catch-all addresses stay separate, unknown addresses need review, and invalid addresses are excluded.

faq.question: What happens when a person changes companies?
faq.answer: The row goes to review and shows both the original company and the current company reported by Leadsets.

faq.question: What happens if the account reaches a limit?
faq.answer: The skill can split the work into batches or process priority rows first. If it stops, it reports which rows remain.

faq.question: Does the skill send emails or update a CRM?
faq.answer: No. It returns CSV files or a Google Sheet through the agent's available connection.
